neighbours.label: concessive hedge phrases that grant a point before a contrast ('of course', 'to be sure', 'to be honest', 'admittedly'); the same sentences without the hedge stay low
fire: The new policy has flaws, of course, but it is better than nothing.
Some voters will object to be sure, yet the measure is likely to pass.
This recipe takes time, of course, and you will need a large pot.
I liked the film overall; to be honest, the ending dragged a little.
The first draft is rough, of course, so expect a few more rounds of edits.
Prices rose sharply last year; to be sure, wages rose as well.
Our team lost again, and to be honest nobody in the stands was surprised.
There are risks involved, of course, but the reward could be large.
quiet: The new policy has flaws, and it will be reviewed again next spring.
Some voters will object loudly, yet the measure is likely to pass.
This recipe takes time, and you will need a large pot.
I liked the film overall; the ending dragged a little.
The first draft is rough, so expect a few more rounds of edits.
Prices rose sharply last year; wages rose as well.
Our team lost again, and nobody in the stands was surprised.
There are risks involved, but the reward could be large.

short: concessive hedge (of course / to be sure)
notes: Card: max 270 on commas before 'but' after a granted claim, plus 'To be honest', 'To be sure', 'of course'. Probe: comma before but 0.027-0.043 (same as comma before and), ', of course,' 0.241, 'To be fair' 0.139. Tests the hedge phrases, not the comma; low confidence.
